name: CA-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Garamendi running with large cash advantage
Republican opponent minimally funded ($235 on hand)
Markets price Democratic win near certain
model.rationale: Garamendi holds a D+19 district with a roughly 50-to-1 fundraising edge, while Recile has essentially no cash and no outside support. Polymarket prices a Democratic win at 97%, consistent with the fundamentals pointing to a safe seat.
model.watch: Any late outside spending or a polling surprise showing a single-digit race would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
John Garamendi, a Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a northern California district that leans Democratic by about 19 points. He enters the general election with roughly $1.2 million on hand after raising nearly $500,000, while Republican Rudy Recile has raised about $20,000 and reports only $235 in cash, with no outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put the Democratic win probability near 97%. The combination of the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the lopsided money gap makes this a Safe Democratic race, with the main uncertainty being the absence of direct polling.
